key_insight: Triangular color codes on Quantinuum’s Helios trapped-ion processor suppressed logical errors by more than an order of magnitude with each tested increase in code distance.
engineering_relevance: Low logical error rates and fast neural-network decoding suggest a path toward fault-tolerant computation with smaller code blocks, though larger-scale operation remains to be demonstrated.
method: Tested distance-3, -5 and -7 triangular color codes with circuit- and hardware-level leakage reduction.
Evaluated encoded two-qubit Clifford randomized benchmarking at distances 3 and 5.
Compared near-optimal algorithmic decoders with convolutional and transformer neural-network decoders.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports logical error rates as low as 5 (+4/−2) × 10⁻⁶, distance-step suppression of 12 (+3/−2), and distance-5 two-qubit Clifford errors of 7 (±3) × 10⁻⁵ per logical Clifford.
watch_item: Results cover small code distances; sustained application-scale performance, including leakage control and real-time decoding at larger distances, remains unproven.
paper_title: Quantum error correction well below the color code threshold
